P1.evidence: No setter. Same compressed three-part frame the rep uses on every call — 'it's just an opportunity for me to understand you. You know, where are you today? Where do you want to be? If we can help, I can go over some options' — missing what is in the way and what you need. No frame agreement sought. Open question ran verbatim: 'How can we potentially help you?'

P2.evidence: The best baseline in the batch, which is a low bar. P2a ran properly and in sequence: 'You're 23. How tall are you?' — '5'7"' — 'And how much do you weigh?' — '160', followed by a useful probe on target weight that surfaced 150 lb as his reference point. Energy was asked directly on P2i and pulled out the work context, which is why P2b scores partial rather than miss. But health conditions and injuries were never asked at all — zero questions in forty-five minutes about anything medical, on a call selling ballistic loaded training to a man who had just said he considers kettlebells dangerous. Diet was never asked; it emerged only when the prospect interrupted the nutrition pillar with 'the most difficult thing for me is the calorie thing.' Sleep was not touched.

P3.evidence: Well run. 'What's the goal for yourself? Is it to just become stronger, get a six-pack, lose fat?' then the sharp follow-up 'You said you're not strong-strong. Why do you want to be strong-strong?' produced the neural-adaptation answer. The bridge ran as 'who do you want to be, say a year from now?' and the rep pushed past the first vague answer with 'you said the best version of yourself and staying there. So what does that best version of Omar look like?' — which produced 'Able, capable, of having my body being functional in the way that it should be.' The ripple was driven all the way through: 'how do you foresee this improving yourself as a man... maybe as a brother?', then the excellent follow-up 'When you said you want to be an image to your little brother and your wife, what do you mean? What do you mean by image?', which reached the brother, the wife, and then the mother and stepfather unprompted. The reflect-back ran properly with the empty-cup frame and was confirmed: 'Is that a good understanding of you and where you're at?' — 'Yep. That's exactly it.' Only P3c is missing.

P4.evidence: P4d and P4e ran well and got the right answer from the prospect's own mouth: 'what do you feel like could really stop you from getting there?' produced 'The knowing, the knowing, the connection', and 'What would you say you need in order to be successful?' produced 'knowledge about what to do... that is structurally full enough for me to grasp'. That is the gap named cleanly. But past attempts were barely explored — the single most important fact, that he had already paid about $1,000 to a coach who never answered his questions, surfaced accidentally twenty-three minutes in during the money isolation and was met with 'Got you' and nothing else. That is the exact objection the programme's access-to-Trevor pillar exists to answer, and it was never connected.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. The two-year question, the settle-for question and the 'why not' were all absent. P5d scores partial on the strength of two adjacent moves: 'Is this a want or a need for you to do this?' followed by 'Why do you say it's a need?', which produced 'I don't think I can keep moving forward and feel at peace without those things'; and 'why are you wanting to take action now... as opposed to doing this in August or September?'. Both are urgency probes rather than cost-of-inaction framing. The prospect had already handed the rep the frame himself — 'when I'm old, it's going to be hard to do it' and 'once those nerve connections stay... when you're old it's hard to come back to it' — and it was never built on. This is the third consecutive call where phase 5 did not run and the subsequent objection had no consequence frame to be returned to.

P6.evidence: The alignment check did run before the price, which is the right order: 'on the scale of one to 10, 10 is I trust these guys to help me. One is I don't feel like I need this.' The answer was positive but not a number — 'Nah, you guys are good. I got a good feeling from y'all' — and the rep took it, following up usefully with 'what gives you that good feeling?' to surface structure and authenticity. But the scripted belief question about getting there with the right structure and the right person was never asked in its own form, and the all-in question ran only later and in its narrower money-isolation version ('money aside, there's nothing else that's stopping you'). P6c is partial: a soft yes existed pre-offer, but when real hesitation arrived — the wife, and then 'I'm going come back to you' — the instruction is to return to phase 5, and instead the rep ran objection B and then took a deposit.

P11.evidence: The only call in this batch where phase 11 is fully observable, and three of its four steps did not happen. Payment: a link was sent in the Zoom chat, the prospect completed a $100 payment and the rep confirmed receipt — 'We got it, bro. You've paid it. We've confirmed it' — but this was a holding deposit, not the programme fee, so P11a is partial. Step 2 was missed: no onboarding call with Trevor was scheduled. The call booked for 5pm the following day is a rebooked sales conversation with the rep himself, and the rep had earlier described the Trevor call as something that happens after purchase. Step 3 was missed entirely — no agreement email, nothing signed. Step 4 was missed entirely — no welcome email, no Skool community link, no onboarding questionnaire. The only email sent was a calendar invitation.

objection_plays.detail: The play ran essentially end to end, in order. Personal conviction confirmed first ('money aside, there's nothing else that's stopping you'). Obstacles anticipated: 'when you guys typically speak about things like this, what do you feel like the potential obstacle could be?'. The would-she-object move: 'why do you feel like she'd want you to become your best self, become stronger?'. Permission-versus-input reframed onto him: 'who's actually responsible for this?' — 'Yeah, me.' And the stuck-path resolution ran exactly as scripted: a deposit plus a refund promise. So by the playbook this is a hit. Two things went beyond the script and should be reviewed as script rather than as rep error. First, an unevidenced closing claim: 'I've had this conversation 2,000 times, dude. You know, when anyone says they speak to their wife, I've never seen anyone come back.' Second, a direct push to pre-commit against his spouse's refusal — 'so even if she says like, hell no, you're still going to do it?' — repeated twice until he answered 'Probably.' Neither move is in the playbook and both are aimed at a 23-year-old who had said 'I'm new to the marriage.'

Isolation ran ('money aside, there's nothing else that's stopping you from really doing this') and the scripted make-it-work invitation ran well — 'if there was a way where we could actually structure this which doesn't take food off your table, which allows you to continue to pay the bills in the house, are you open to actually moving forward?'. Of the financial picture he obtained monthly surplus after bills (~$1,000), credit score (700), one credit card and its available limit ($200). He did not ask cash on hand — the $800-1,000 figure was volunteered — did not ask how many cards, did not ask used versus available, and did not ask about investments. The play was then resolved not by financing the published product but by a twelve-month structure whose arithmetic does not reconcile with the quoted price.

Doubt was live in two forms. The stated one, attributed to his wife, was 'is it going to work? Like, is it something that good to invest on it?', which the rep met correctly with the scripted closing move: 'how would you know that this is going to work or not if you don't actually try it?'. But the BURNED BEFORE move — which exists in the playbook precisely for this — was never run, despite the prospect having disclosed that he already lost about $1,000 to a coach who ignored him. The certainty question, the pleasure-versus-pain question, the BRIDGE and the PLANE were all absent. Started, and the most applicable move left on the table.
He did not ask for thinking time in substance; the deferral was specifically to consult his wife and is scored under OB.
Timing was never raised as a blocker; he wanted to start immediately.

Safety objection with no scripted play, and it was stated twice unprompted: 'I've always wanted to do the kettlebell thing, but I see it as dangerous, you know?' and, of his wife, 'she was interested in kettlebells before, but I was like, no, we're going to get hurt.' Neither was acknowledged at any point in the call. The playbook has no move for a prospect who believes the modality itself will injure him, and no baseline question that would surface it — the same structural hole as the clinical-fit gap already logged, approached from the prospect's side rather than a clinician's. Worth adding: it is also the most obvious value hook available here, since form coaching is precisely the answer to it.

Provider-trust objection from a previous bad purchase: 'I invested like a thousand in this coaching with this person, but they didn't guide me... I asked questions and no response.' There is no scripted play for re-establishing trust after a failed coaching purchase, and the rep did not improvise one — he said 'Got you' and moved on. This is a distinct gap from the cheaper-alternative one already on the known list, and it recurs across the corpus wherever prospects have bought online coaching before.

notes: Strong phase 3 again and the only properly sequenced baseline in the batch, but the same two structural failures: no consequence frame, and hesitation resolved by restructuring money rather than by returning to phase 5. Phase 11 is fully visible here for once and three of its four steps were skipped — no Trevor call, no agreement, no welcome sequence — which suggests the onboarding checklist is not being run even when payment happens on camera. Two items for the business rather than for coaching: the objection B play as written ends in a deposit-plus-refund, and here that produced a $100 payment from a junior soldier with $800 to his name on the strength of an unwritten refund promise; and the quoted instalment figures do not reconcile with the quoted totals.
